# 3 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** The Royal Decree Against the Jews

---

**3:1** Now when Ptolemy had learned of these things, and was informed that the Jews were firmly resolved and would not submit to his edicts — having heard also that some of them were favorably disposed toward him and that many had remained completely devoted to him — he gave orders that no change was to be made in their attitude but that they were to be kept in custody under guard, and securely bound in every direction with bonds of iron, and on no account were they to receive any assistance or comfort.

**3:2** Moreover in addition to all this, by his command the Jews were stripped of all their possessions and rights of citizenship.

**3:3** Furthermore they were not permitted to draw water from wells, and were not allowed any of the other benefits of life.

**3:4** And all this was done by means of a decree made by the royal power, as befits a king without reason or wisdom.

**3:5** But when information about these things reached the Jews' friends, since many of the Alexandrians had friendly relations with them, they went to visit them secretly, giving them provisions and consoling them.

**3:6** And they were given hope by the news, and the Alexandrians also promised that they would do whatever they could to get them freed.

**3:7** Then Ptolemy, having given further orders, commanded that this nation, the Jews, be gathered together into one place and brought to him under guard.

**3:8** He also commanded that any persons of standing who refused to comply with his orders regarding the Jews and desired to help them should be punished with death.

**3:9** When these measures had been carried out and much had been done against the Jews with every kind of violence and cruelty, there arose among all the people of Judea those who longed to help the Jews and to stand by them.

**3:10** Then the king, puffed up with great arrogance, and inflated with the drunkenness of his power, wrote to the following effect.

**3:11** King Ptolemy Philopator, to the commanders and soldiers throughout Egypt and all its territories, greetings. I am in good health, and my affairs are in order.

**3:12** After the expedition to Asia and the return, through the goodwill of the gods and the good fortune that has attended our affairs, we have now determined — not through the use of force but through goodwill — to devote ourselves to the service of the gods of the land.

**3:13** Since the Jews continue to maintain ill-will toward us and have not submitted to our rule, and since they showed contempt for our sacred places and stirred up disturbances in our kingdom,

**3:14** we have resolved to deal with them accordingly and to punish them publicly for their lawless behavior.

**3:15** We give you instructions as follows: all the Jews of your district are to be transported to Alexandria under arrest and brought to us under guard.

**3:16** They are not to be treated with any compassion or pity whatsoever.

**3:17** We are confident that all these enemies of our power have been conquered and that our authority over them is complete.

**3:18** When they arrive in Alexandria they are to be punished with torture and death.

**3:19** And in this way we will eradicate the whole race of these men from among us.

**3:20** All their property will become the king's possession.

**3:21** Any person who shelters a Jew will be put to death.

**3:22** We are sending a copy of this letter throughout the land so that it may not be hidden from anyone and so that all may know of our command and may be prepared to carry it out without fail.
